cards.front: Does continuous learning mean taking a course every week?
cards.back: No. It means keeping curiosity and updating the knowledge that supports decisions, without turning free time into an extension of the workday.

cards.front: Does moving into management remove the need to learn?
cards.back: No. People who lead also have to follow changes in the work, understand the team, and decide in contexts that evolve.

cards.front: Does AI take responsibility for what it delivers?
cards.back: No. The tool can collaborate, but responsibility for the decision stays with people and with the organization.

cards.front: What does learning to use AI include, besides writing good prompts?
cards.back: Giving context, recognizing limits, checking sources, protecting data, and spotting when a convincing answer is wrong. Also knowing when to solve something without it.

cards.front: Does keeping up with the profession require knowing every new tool?
cards.back: No. It requires solid fundamentals and criteria for choosing the next thing to learn, without living in permanent urgency.

cards.front: Which question helps choose what to learn now?
cards.back: What do I need to learn now in order to do my work better and make more conscious decisions?

cards.front: When would we be slaves to technology?
cards.back: If we accepted every novelty as an order, with no room to choose, question, or set limits.

cards.front: Who is the professional who grows in this discussion?
cards.back: Not necessarily the one who uses more tools or studies more hours. It is the one who connects knowledge, context, and responsibility in order to create value.
